source: H. G. Wells, The Time Machine (1895), Project Gutenberg eBook #35
passages: The Time Traveller pushed his glass towards the Silent Man and rang it with his fingernail; at which the Silent Man, who had been staring at his face, started convulsively, and poured him wine.
Although it was at my own expense, I could not help myself. I laughed aloud.

I determined to put the thought of my Time Machine and the mystery of the bronze doors under the sphinx, as much as possible in a corner of memory, until my growing knowledge would lead me back to them in a natural way.
I had to think rapidly what to do. I determined to build a fire and encamp where we were.
All trace of the moon had vanished. The circling of the stars, growing slower and slower, had given place to creeping points of light.
There were no breakers and no waves, for not a breath of wind was stirring.
The hands spun backward upon the dials. At last I saw again the dim shadows of houses, the evidences of decadent humanity.
There was a momentary stillness. Then chairs began to creak and shoes to scrape upon the carpet.
